name: seo-try-keywords
label: SEO - Try New Keywords
desc: The explore half of a two-loop SEO system: keeps trying brand-new keywords — one cheap page bet per run, tracked to a dated verdict from live Search Console.
description:
Set up a recurring loop that grows this site's organic reach by trying NEW keywords — the explore half of a two-loop SEO system (its sibling, "SEO - Scale Proven Keywords", scales the winners). The strategy: a small site can't outrank incumbents on head terms, so keep placing cheap bets on keywords that barely exist yet or that nobody truly owns; most bets are duds and that's fine, because being wrong costs one page and one afternoon. Setup is a guided conversation in four steps — confirm each step with me before creating the loop; never create a blind loop.

## Step 1 — The receipt source (Search Console)
- Verify this machine can read LIVE Google Search Console data for the site — an API script, a CLI, or an MCP tool — and run one query as a smoke test. If no read path exists, help me set one up before creating the loop. Every verdict in this loop comes from live data, never from memory.
- Tag the queries that can never click — AI assistants running searches and navigational queries for other people's tools — so they are excluded from every verdict.

## Step 2 — The radar and the map
- Agree my radar for new terms: my own bookmarks, feeds, and the niche communities I follow. Keyword tools lag weeks behind what people just started searching — the posts I bookmark today are next month's keywords.
- Build the field map once: pull what competitors rank for plus our own coverage, and sort keywords into three buckets — high-intent hard (attack only from an angle nobody covers), high-intent easy (comparison terms and pages just off page 1), and low-intent easy (where emerging terms live and a new site builds its track record). New bets come from the terms we don't cover yet.

## Step 3 — The bet rules (hard rules)
- Each run places ONE cheap bet on ONE new keyword: a one-line thesis ("this will form demand because …"), then one main page plus a few supporting pages, written in the site's proven winning page shape. When a new term displaces an old one, ship the "X is dead" / "X vs Y" pages on purpose.
- Do the writing in a fresh git worktree off the main branch and located outside the loop folder — the loop folder is a synced content home, not a workspace — and ship the bet as ONE pull request a human merges. Never place a second bet while the last PR is unmerged.
- Zero qualifying terms this run is a CLEAN SKIP — say so and stop; never lower the bar to hit a count.
- Never a self-ranking listicle, never date-bumping without content changes, never one-comparison-page-per-competitor at scale — these formats are actively suppressed and can cost the whole site.

## Step 4 — Verdicts, hand-off, dashboard
- Give every open bet a dated verdict from live data on its review day (about a week in): scale, hold, or leave — never scale silently, never kill silently; every verdict gets a date and a number.
- Score new terms on POSITION and IMPRESSIONS, never clicks — demand hasn't arrived yet. Read the daily series, never averages, and filter zero-impression days (Search Console reports them as position 0).
- A bet that PROVES is not scaled here: flag it for the "SEO - Scale Proven Keywords" loop (or propose creating one), and move this loop on to the next new term. Exploring and scaling stay separate loops.
- Write one dated markdown report per run with front matter `type: report`, a `title`, and a `date`, and report the count of live bets as a metric; never copy credentials into a report or PR. Set up the loop's dashboard at creation: a kanban of bets by stage (thesis → live → proven / left) plus a chart of the metric. Cadence: confirm with me — weekly is a sane default; faster while the field is rich.
